text:
Kai: FYI seeing a p99 jump on prod-gpu pool starting ~04:12 UTC, ~3x on short-seq traffic. I captured a couple of traces, looks like kernel autoselect is falling back to a slower flash kernel path when KV cache pressure + mem fragmentation coincide.

Maria: ugh, any concrete evidence? graphs/links?

Kai: quick summary + paste from triton selector/logs:
```
2026-03-18T04:12:14Z [selector] model=gptx seq=512 batch=8 chosen=flash_attn_fp16_v2 fallback=true reason=shared_mem_unavailable
2026-03-18T04:12:14Z [runtime] kv_cache_eviction rate=0.12 p50_evicted_tokens=64
P99 latency baseline=95ms -> incident=330ms, throughput ~-18%
```

Cheng: we rolled nvidia driver 535.86 to that fleet yesterday morning — could be changed SMEM layout or driver allocator behavior. saw fragmentation on one host when reproducing locally.

Jess: any noisy neighbor containers on those hosts? if other customers/teams have large pinned allocations, that can blow up fragmentation and make kernels pick lower-SMEM variants.

Kai: saw this in nvidia-smi on the affected node: 
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes: GPU Memory |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                   Usage |
|    0  8921 C   python /opt/services/batch-infer        28.4GiB |
|    0 10342 C   python /opt/runtime/serve               10.2GiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
batch-infer had a big transient allocation during a nightly job at ~04:10 which coincides.

Maria: @Kai did you run a microprofile (nsight/nvprof) of the slow path?

Kai: yes, nvprof snapshot shows a drop in occupancy and extra global memory ops (spill) for the chosen kernel vs baseline:
```
Kernel: flash_attn_fp16_v2  |  avg time 1.6ms -> 4.8ms (per tile)
metrics: achieved_occupancy 0.43 -> 0.18, shared_load_replays ++, local_load_replays ++
callstack shows selector flagged smem_unavailable at runtime->kernel_launcher.cpp:412
```

Cheng: that matches a change in the driver's allocator heuristic — when fragmentation prevents contiguous smem/implicit scratch, Triton selector marks some optimized kernels invalid and picks a more conservative kernel (higher register/shared usage).

Jess: mitigation ideas?

Kai: short term options: 1) revert driver on affected nodes (hard for prod), 2) force kernel_autoselect to prefer smaller-smem kernel variant for seq<=512 via runtime config (can patch quickly), 3) add aggressive KV alignment allocator so we don't fragment SMEM layout, 4) schedule nightly large-batch jobs to different nodes (workaround).

Maria: can we do a canary for option 2? patch config in a canary row of 3 nodes and run the workload generator. Also add a guardrail to revert if latency degrades.

deploy-bot: Deploy request submitted by Kai for config:runtime.kernel_autoselect.prefer_small_smem=true to canary pool (3 nodes).

ops-bot: Canary deploy started at 04:27 UTC (canary-pool-3).

Cheng: also adding instrumentation: log selector.reason and chosen_variant to metrics so we can chart fallback frequency per node and per 1h window. That will help confirm root cause (fragmentation -> fallback).

Kai: test command I ran to repro locally: 
```
./runtime/profiler --model gptx --seq 512 --batch 8 --iters 200 --trace-selector --nvprof-out=/tmp/prof.nvprof
```
Use that against canary nodes.

Jess: long term we should: 1) upstream allocator patch (aligned arena for KV pages), 2) add kernel scoring penalty for fallback churn (avoid oscillation), 3) driver / runtime compatibility tests in CI that simulate fragmented allocations.

Maria: agreed. For now, keep canary for 30m and if p99 < 120ms and fallback rate down, roll to rest of fleet. If not, revert and consider targeted driver rollback for the most critical customers.

Kai: I'll post the small perf dashboard link and nvprof artifacts to the incident doc after canary finishes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
